title: Isandro and the Sigil Anew
premise: Jonah Sandoval, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-free city of Vessengard, discovers that the old gods are answering prayers again — and that her own exile was engineered by the covenant's original betrayer, Chancellor Isandro Vael. As divine power floods back into the world, it corrupts those who grasp it too greedily, and Jonah must gather a found family of outcasts to reforge the broken covenant between mortal and divine realms. At the climax she refuses the gods' offer to make her their sole vessel, choosing instead a covenant of shared power, and shatters Isandro's bid to become the thirteenth god before the moon completes its final turn. The book ends with Jonah, no longer exiled, choosing to remain in Vessengard as its first licensed storm-caller — family, not power, as her homecoming.
about_author: Ines Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who inherit broken things and decide to mend them anyway.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Jonah Sandoval sells harmless trinkets in Vessengard, concealing the storm-scar on her palm that marks her exile. When a desperate widow's prayer is answered by something ancient, Jonah feels her dormant power stir. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the weary comfort of a hidden life beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: An astronomer named Pell Wicke shows Jonah that the moon has begun an impossible thirteenth turn in a single year — an omen recorded only before the last covenant war. The city's Chancellery begins arresting 'prayer-criminals.' POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Jonah seeks out Brannoc, a disgraced temple-keeper living under the aqueduct, who confirms the gods are waking — and that her exile twelve years ago was no accident. He gives her a shard of the broken covenant sigil. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: betrayal resurfacing as grief.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Smile
chapters.summary: Isandro Vael, the beloved Chancellor who outlawed magic, publicly pardons Jonah in a calculated gesture, inviting her to the Chancellery. She recognizes his voice from the night her covenant-circle burned. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: terror wearing the mask of civility.

chapters.title: A Thief with Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Sefa, a pickpocket who can briefly touch the divine residue on objects, tries to steal Jonah's sigil shard and instead becomes her unlikely ally. Their bickering partnership reveals Sefa's own stolen history. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: loneliness meeting its match.

chapters.title: The God Who Answers Wrong
chapters.summary: A minor god, half-mad from twelve godless years, grants a mob's prayers with catastrophic literalism. Jonah uses her storm-calling for the first time since exile to save a tenement, exposing herself publicly. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: power remembered as both joy and danger.

chapters.title: Wanted: Storm-Caller
chapters.summary: Branded a criminal, Jonah flees with Sefa and Brannoc into the Godsfen wetlands, where exiled faithful have built a hidden sanctuary. Old resentments greet her — some blame her circle's fall for the ban. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: exile within exile, and the first fragile welcome.

chapters.title: The Cartography of Prayer
chapters.summary: Pell, now a fugitive, arrives with maps showing where the covenant sigil's fragments fell across the realm. Reforging it requires a bearer willing to carry each fragment's burden — a burden that reshapes the bearer. POV: Pell. Emotional beat: hope arriving with a price tag.

chapters.title: Salt and Ember
chapters.summary: The first fragment, held by a drowned god's remnant in the fen, tests Jonah with visions of her old circle — including the friend who betrayed them to Isandro. She takes the fragment and it brands her arm. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: forgiveness attempted, not yet achieved.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Cathedral
chapters.summary: Isandro unveils a grand cathedral to 'the god of order' — himself, fed by siphoned divine power. He offers Jonah restoration of her full name and rights if she serves as his storm-engine. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: corruption dressed as mercy, and the seduction of belonging.

chapters.title: What Sefa Saw in the Dark
chapters.summary: Sefa infiltrates the cathedral and discovers Isandro was Jonah's circle-mate, the betrayer, now consuming gods to become the thirteenth. She barely escapes with proof. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by the fear of what truth does to Jonah.

chapters.title: The Weight of the Second Shard
chapters.summary: In the mountains, the second fragment's guardian is a god who demands a memory as payment. Jonah surrenders her memory of her mother's face, and the group sees her grief change her. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: witness as an act of love.

chapters.title: Moonturn
chapters.summary: The moon completes its twelfth turn; the sky visibly wrongs itself. Isandro's agents attack the sanctuary, and Brannoc dies holding the fen gate so the others can escape with the fragments. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: found family paying its first blood-price.

chapters.title: Ashes, Argued Over
chapters.summary: Grief fractures the group: Pell blames Jonah's fame, Sefa defends her, and Jonah nearly takes Isandro's earlier offer. In the ruins of her old circle's meetinghouse, she chooses to continue. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the dark night where quitting looks reasonable.

chapters.title: The Third Fragment Sings
chapters.summary: The third fragment lies in the sea-god's drowned cathedral, guarded by a choir of the dead faithful. Sefa's gift lets her hear the covenant's original words, and she sings them back to open the way. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: the thief becoming the key.

chapters.title: Thirteen Gods, Twelve Thrones
chapters.summary: Pell deciphers the covenant's full text: it was never about controlling the gods but sharing power among thirteen — and Isandro means to take the empty thirteenth seat alone. The moon's thirteenth turn is his coronation clock. POV: Pell. Emotional beat: understanding the enemy's logic, and refusing it.

chapters.title: The Offer Refused
chapters.summary: The waking gods offer Jonah godhood as their vessel — the easy path to defeating Isandro. She refuses, knowing a single vessel is just another Isandro, and asks instead for partnership. Some gods rage; one, the fen's drowned remnant, agrees. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: power declined, identity claimed.

chapters.title: Storm Over Vessengard
chapters.summary: Jonah returns to the city openly, rallying the faithful and the fearful alike as Isandro's coronation begins under the full thirteenth moon. Sefa's stolen proof turns public opinion in the streets. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: the exiles coming home as a family.

chapters.title: The Betrayer's Crown
chapters.summary: In the cathedral, Isandro ascends toward the thirteenth throne, consuming the lesser gods mid-ritual. Jonah confronts him with the memory of their circle, forcing him to falter — but he takes the throne anyway, and the sky tears. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the villain's grief revealed too late to save him.

chapters.title: The Sigil Anew
chapters.summary: Climax: Jonah, Sefa, Pell, and the allied gods reforge the covenant sigil together, each bearing a fragment's burden — shared, not hoarded. Jonah calls the storm not as a weapon but as a bridge, unmaking Isandro's stolen divinity and resealing the realms. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: power distributed, corruption broken.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns, Then Rest
chapters.summary: The moon returns to its natural course. Jonah is offered a seat among the renewed covenant's mortal voices and declines it, choosing the city instead. She buries Brannoc's ashes in the fen and takes Sefa and Pell to dinner like ordinary people. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: quiet after the storm, home chosen freely.

chapters.title: Charms for a City That Remembers
chapters.summary: Epilogue: a year later, Jonah's shop sells real charms under license, and a frightened young magic-born girl knocks on her door. Jonah recognizes herself and leaves the sign open. The sigil shard on her shelf hums, content. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the found family becoming a doorway for the next exile.
